learning: If the oval finish rate is at or above about 0.5, the iteration 1 reference is stable and later changes can be judged against it. If it is well below 0.5, the reference was partly seed luck, so compare future designs over several seeds before accepting a change.
notes: Reproduces the iteration 1 best design exactly, with the same controller, so this race tests repeatability of the reference. Any change in outcome comes from seed variance, not from a design change.
rationale: The Builder's proposal returns to the iteration 1 geometry: 0.8 kg mass, 0.12 m wheel_track, 0.12 m wheel radius, 0.12 x 0.16 m body, 12 mm sensors on the widened row at x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, y = 0.04 m. Iteration 1 is still the best raced design (324.07, oval finish rate 0.70, oval steering_oscillation 0.26). Every later change was worse on the oval: 16 mm sensors (0.00 finishes), wheel_track 0.10 m with kp 4.5 (0.10), mass 0.6 kg (0.30) and mass 0.7 kg (0.15). The 0.7 kg point is non-monotonic, and the evidence does not support a new optimum, so I hold the geometry exactly. The controller is also unchanged from iteration 1 (kp 5.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.6, base_speed 1.2, last_direction, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]). Changing gains now would confound the repeatability test. The off-track limit is 0.06 m, and iteration 1 s-bend and slalom max_error sat at about 0.064 m, so those tracks will likely not complete; the score depends mainly on the oval. Expected result, not measured: oval finish rate about 0.5 to 0.7, mean score near 300, with wide seed variance. If the oval finish rate falls well below 0.5, the iteration 1 result was partly seed luck and future changes should be judged on multi-seed averages.
